steps.title: Key Facts
steps.body: Bristol is a city in south-west England with a population of approximately 470,000 (wider metro area 725,000). It is the largest city in the South West and the 8th largest in England. It has a diverse economy, two universities, and a rich cultural heritage. Bristol was European Green Capital in 2015.

steps.title: Geography Exam Tips — Urban Change in the UK
steps.body: 1. For Urban Change in the UK questions, always name specific case studies with factual detail 2. Use geographical terminology precisely (e.g. specific processes, not vague descriptions) 3. Consider social, economic and environmental perspectives in your evaluations 4. Support your points about Urban Change in the UK with data, statistics or named examples 5. For 'assess' or 'evaluate' questions, reach a clear judgement supported by evidence

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how international migration has affected a named UK city. (4 marks) | Describe two challenges of urban change in a named UK city. (4 marks) | Using a named UK city, assess the impact of urban regeneration. (6 marks)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use Bristol as your named UK city case study - know specific facts and figures Always link migration impacts to specific communities (Somali in Easton, Polish in St Paul's) For regeneration, evaluate who benefits and who might be disadvantaged Know the inequality contrast: Clifton vs Lawrence Hill (10-year life expectancy gap) Use Temple Quarter and Harbourside as specific regeneration examples Always consider social, economic and environmental impacts in your answers
